findings.title: Double interpolation risk: runSplitQuery now applies template variables, but callers may already have interpolated queries
findings.body: runSplitQuery now calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables on each target unconditionally. shardQuerySplitting.ts's runShardSplitQuery also independently applies applyTemplateVariables before calling splitQueriesByStreamShard, which internally calls runSplitQuery (via subRequest). If runSplitQuery is reached with already-interpolated queries from the sharding path, applyTemplateVariables will be invoked a second time on an already-interpolated expr/step, which can corrupt expressions containing literal '$' characters or already-substituted template variables (e.g., if a label value itself contains a '$' sequence that happens to match a variable syntax). This also changes the datasource.query() entrypoint behavior if it previously relied on interpolation happening elsewhere exactly once.

findings.title: Non-splitting/instant queries now go through applyTemplateVariables unconditionally, bypassing prior per-call-path interpolation contracts
findings.body: Previously, interpolation timing/ownership was handled by callers (e.g., datasource.query or specific splitting functions). Now querySplitting.ts interpolates every non-hidden, non-empty query up front for all code paths (logs, metric, non-splitting). If any caller already interpolates before invoking runSplitQuery (a plausible existing contract elsewhere in the codebase not shown in this diff), this introduces silent double-interpolation bugs that are hard to detect via type-checking since applyTemplateVariables is idempotent only for already-resolved queries without conflicting variable names docs/tests don't cover this scenario.
